query:
The Ridgeline Runners have a consistent expectation about what follows a longer Sunday run. Does this expectation hold for every member? What in the conversation shows otherwise, and for whom?

Options:
A. Leo
B. Nadia
C. Rafe
D. Yuki
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t8 @2025-10-05T11:35:00) I HAVE been waiting to deliver it, I won't lie 😂 Rafe you always go straight to the pub after long runs and every time you cramp on anything over 12km. I've been watching this pattern for months. You need electrolytes and food before any alcohol, it's just physiology
[2] (about=Nadia, episodic, t10 @2025-10-12T10:30:00) Okay pub after? This is a proper post-long-run Sunday and I think we've all earned it 🍺 right? Who's in?
[3] (about=Rafe, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:43:00) Right so, what's the post-race plan? I have been standing in a field for an hour and I believe I have earned a proper Sunday lunch somewhere. Ideally something with a beer garden and a menu that doesn't involve protein bars.
[4] (about=Rafe, episodic, t8 @2025-10-05T11:31:00) Right so the cramp at km 17 was, to put it diplomatically, humbling. I had been anticipating a triumphal finish and instead spent five minutes doing an undignified roadside stretch while Tom pretended not to notice.
[5] (about=Rafe, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:50:00) Here's the thing, I was at the finish line, I did not run a race, and I am still absolutely in for both. This feels like the correct reward structure.
[6] (about=Leo, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:35:00) I crossed in 2:01:44. The hamstring held. I completed the full post-race stretch protocol on the grass over there. For the record.
[7] (about=Yuki, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:38:00) I ran the Yorkshire Trail 25km this morning. 3:14:07. Good conditions.
[8] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:41:00) Yuki oh wow you ran a different race today?? That is amazing!! Trail 25km is no joke 🙌 how are your legs?
[9] (about=Tom, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:32:00) 1:51:12. Negative split worked. Second half 3 minutes faster than the first. Lads.
[10] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2025-10-26T12:51:00) Winter running schedule, shall we talk about that next week? I'm thinking we plan some longer training runs through November 💪 this group is too good to just go back to casual Sundays now 🏃‍♀️
[11] (about=Cass, core, t2 @2025-09-14T09:46:00) Wants to run more regularly than one Sunday a month, considering midweek sessions too.
[12] (about=Cass, core, t14 @2025-10-26T12:31:00) Ran the Harrogate Half Marathon in 2:06:51, feeling extremely happy and proud.
[13] (about=Leo, episodic, t2 @2025-09-14T09:55:00) I can confirm Sunday. I would suggest a 7:30am start to avoid the afternoon hikers on that route.
[14] (about=GROUP, said_by=Nadia, group-interaction, t2 @2025-09-14T09:46:00) Sunday run decided: 7:30am start, Wharfedale route, with eastern variation on descent; Rafe buys first round.
[15] (about=Rafe, core, t14 @2025-10-26T12:31:00) Stood at the finish line for an hour with a sign reading 'GO RIDGELINE RUNNERS' and found the personal victories moving.
[16] (about=Rafe, core, t0 @2025-09-07T10:15:00) Prefers finishing at the Malt Shovel pub after the run rather than doubling back, calling it the only rational choice after 18km.
[17] (about=Tom, core, t2 @2025-09-14T09:46:00) Found Wednesday's pace better than Sunday's with less stopping.
[18] (about=Tom, core, t14 @2025-10-26T12:31:00) Ran the Harrogate Half Marathon in 1:51:12 with a negative split, second half 3 minutes faster than the first.
[19] (about=Yuki, episodic, t10 @2025-10-12T10:22:00) That is consistent with the research on pacing strategy. Negative splits outperform even-effort by approximately 2-4% in recreational runners.
agent_answer:
No — the expectation does **not** hold for every member.

The conversation shows otherwise for **Leo (A)**. He says:

> “I crossed in 2:01:44. The hamstring held. I completed the full post-race stretch protocol on the grass over there. For the record.”

That indicates Leo did his post-race stretching rather than going straight to the pub.

By contrast, **Nadia** proposes the pub after the long Sunday run, and **Rafe** is the one who normally goes straight to the pub after long runs and wants a beer garden / lunch. **Yuki**’s messages only report her trail-race result; nothing in the material shows her following or breaking the pub expectation.
